sources: dossier=Required behaviors 'graphs: block, reserved main...' (2026-05-15, artifact-only) does not claim graphs: is the exclusive declaration surface; doc=graph.md:11 said templates declare graphs 'uniformly via the template DSL's graphs surface'; code=template_validator_graphs.go:14-20 canonicalizeGraphs early-returns (zero errors) when spec.Graphs is empty, so a flat top-level nodes: template validates cleanly; test=TestCanonicalizeGraphs_FlatShape_NoIsSubgraphExit (template_validator_graphs_test.go:454) asserts zero errors for a Graphs-less spec; examples/ has 21 nodes:-form templates and 0 graphs:-form templates.
note: The dossier is silent on whether the flat top-level nodes: form remains legitimate, but design corpus corroboration (a dedicated passing unit test plus 100% of examples/ using the flat form, plus a validator error message that itself says 'use one form (graphs: preferred)') establishes it as a deliberate, currently-supported alternative, not an oversight. Doc rewritten to describe both forms; applied alongside row 64's fix to the same passage.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors 'graphs: block, reserved main...' (2026-05-15, artifact-only) never states that every template must explicitly declare a graphs: block; doc=graph.md:19 'Every template must declare the reserved top-level graph'; code=canonicalizeGraphs (template_validator_graphs.go:18-20) only emits subgraph_missing_main inside the graphs:-populated branch, so flat nodes:-only templates register with zero graphs declared and frame/producer.go:32 stamps the root run-scope's GraphName to MainGraphName unconditionally, making the flat template implicitly the main graph; test=TestCanonicalizeGraphs_FlatShape_NoIsSubgraphExit shows zero validation errors for a Graphs-less spec.
note: As literally written the invariant is false today: 100% of examples/ templates (flat nodes:-only) would fail it, an implausible state for a maintained example suite, and the passing unit test plus the unconditional MainGraphName stamp corroborate that the flat form implicitly constitutes the reserved graph rather than violating a declaration requirement. Rescoped the invariant to state the reserved graph always exists (explicit or implicit) rather than claiming mandatory explicit declaration.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors 'graphs: block, reserved main as the reserved top-level graph' (2026-05-15, artifact-only) names the reserved graph 'main'; doc=graph.md previously said only 'A reserved top-level graph name designates the instance-level graph' without stating the literal; code=lib/foundation/spec/graphs.go MainGraphName = "main"; design corpus=sub-graph.md's own invariant names 'The `main` graph' explicitly, establishing that DSL literals are admissible prose in this doc family.
note: The owning concept withheld a literal a neighbor concept already states; multiple independent artifacts (dossier, code constant, neighbor doc) agree the name is main. Doc updated to name main directly wherever the reserved graph is referenced.

sources: dossier=Net position 'Instance wake is message-driven: an empty message is the root trigger, with structural root-edge injection at registration and instance-create-is-idle; the synthetic-envelope wake mechanism is retired' (2026-06-17, transcript) and Intentional absences 'Synthetic-envelope wake mechanism ... retired' (2026-06-17, daf59a14, transcript); doc=graph.md:11,19 said 'every instance binds its state machine to that top-level graph' / 'The instance state machine is bound to it'; design corpus=grep across concepts/ finds only node-run.md's seven-state machine defined; instance.md defines no instance-level state machine; code=frame/producer.go:32 stamps the root run-scope's GraphName to MainGraphName (a run-scope binding, not a state-machine binding).
note: Transcript-tier dossier evidence confirms the wake/instance-creation model was reworked away from any instance-level state-machine framing toward message-driven root run-scope binding; 'instance state machine' is undefined stale terminology pointing a reader at a nonexistent artifact. Replaced with 'instance's root run-scope binds to that top-level graph', matching the corroborating code and dossier framing.

sources: dossier=silent on sub-graph node materialization timing; doc=graph.md:21 said sub-graph definitions 'are never instantiated directly at instance creation'; design corpus=node.md:25 'The rimsky_nodes row is set at instance creation' establishes 'instantiated' as this catalog's vocabulary for per-instance node-row creation; code=canonicalizeGraphs' flatten (template_validator_graphs.go:136-184) merges every sub-graph's nodes into the persisted spec.Nodes list, and instances.go:909-938 loops over tpl.Spec.Nodes creating a persistence row for every node, including flattened sub-graph internals.
note: Under the vocabulary node.md establishes, sub-graph nodes ARE instantiated (row-created) at instance creation; the doc's real claim is that they are never dispatched/run except via delegation. Rewrote the invariant to say sub-graph nodes are never dispatched except through delegation and carry no independent entry point, avoiding the 'instantiated' collision with concept:node's established meaning.
